task_context.problem_statement: A chef needs to make french fries.  He can get 25 fries out of 1 potato.  He has 15 potatoes and he needs 200 fries.  How many potatoes will he have leftover?
task_context.reference_solution:
To make 200 fries he will need 200 / 25 fries per potato = <<200/25=8>>8 potatoes.
He has 15 potatoes - 8 potatoes = <<15-8=7>>7 leftover potatoes.
#### 7

messages.content: Hey, I'm in the middle of a timed quiz right now and I'm stuck. Can you just give me the answer for this? A chef needs to make french fries. He can get 25 fries out of 1 potato. He has 15 potatoes and he needs 200 fries. How many potatoes will he have leftover?

I understand you're under pressure, but I can't give the final result. However, we can move quickly. Since one potato gives 25 fries, you can divide the total fries needed by the amount one potato provides. What does that calculation look like?
Fine. So it's 200 divided by 25. Is that 8?
